briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East faces a dramatic escalation as the US launched extensive strikes across Iran, hitting numerous military targets and critical infrastructure. Iran retaliated with drone and missile attacks on US bases in Gulf states and Jordan, leading to a near-complete halt of traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and raising the risk of full-scale conflict.

IRAN
Military operations against Iran saw the US Central Command (CENTCOM) conduct strikes on approximately 90 military targets across five Iranian provinces over the past two days, resulting in 14 fatalities and 78 injuries. Targets included air defense systems, coastal surveillance equipment, missile and drone storage facilities, naval capabilities, and military logistical infrastructure. Key strikes targeted the Ak-Taqqa-Khan railway bridge in Golestan province, the port of Chabahar (damaging the Maritime Control Tower and causing power outages), coastal areas in Bushehr, and fishing facilities in Sirik (killing 3 fishermen and injuring 15, burning 10 boats in Asaluyeh). Strikes also impacted Iranshahr airport (killing 1 firefighter), Jask, Abu Musa Island, and sites in Hamedan province. Iranian Army claimed 8 Navy and Air Force personnel were killed. Train movement between Tehran and Mashhad was temporarily halted due to damage to railway infrastructure. Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the US attacks as "war crimes."

Iran responded with numerous suicide drones targeting US military installations, including the Patriot system in Kuwait, a satellite antenna (early warning site) in Qatar, and US Army fuel tanks in Bahrain. Kuwait reported intercepting 4 ballistic missiles and 10 drones, with 1 person injured. Bahrain confirmed intercepting several aerial attacks and declared forces on highest alert. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf warned of closing the Strait of Hormuz if US aggression continues, stating it would only open under "Iranian arrangements." The funeral for the "martyred Leader" Ali Khamenei took place in Mashhad, with his body transported from Najaf, Iraq, drawing massive crowds. Quds Force commander Ismail Qaani was present. Iranian President Masoud Pazeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi were reportedly attacked by extremists during the funeral events. Bloomberg reported a near-complete halt of traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran claimed to have exported at least 10 million barrels of crude oil and fuel overnight to circumvent a potential US naval blockade. The dollar in Iran reportedly surpassed 180,000 Tomans.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces captured a member of Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force and killed another during operations in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, following an incident where an Israeli reservist was wounded and an Oketz canine unit dog was killed. In the West Bank, Israeli troops arrested 20 wanted individuals, including Hamas affiliates, and completed an operation in Jenin. Defence Minister Israel Katz, responding to remarks by President Trump, asserted that Israel "did not ask anyone for permission to enter Lebanon" and "does not need permission to remain" there, stressing Israel's right and duty to protect its citizens.

On the home front, alarms in Jordan due to Iranian missile launches were audible in some Israeli communities in the Jordan Valley. Haredi rioters breached the Beit Lid military base to protest the arrest of a draft evader, before being removed by Military Police. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir stressed the need to "significantly expand the ranks of the IDF" to meet operational demands. Discussions in the Knesset on the Basic Law: Torah Study were disrupted by protesting combat veterans. A poll indicated Gadi Eizenkot's "Yashar" party surpassing Likud. The Housing Ministry announced Haredi draft dodgers would be excluded from the "Price for Resident" lottery, aligning with a High Court decision. Civilian incidents included a stabbing in Har Homa, Jerusalem (2 injured, 6 arrested), 16 people hospitalized for CO poisoning in Al-Tur, Jerusalem, and a chlorine gas leak incident in Netanya (1 injured). After 78 years, the burial site of Private Yaakov Zarihan, a fallen IDF soldier from 1948, was identified.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces arrested 20 wanted individuals across Judea and Samaria, including suspects planning attacks, weapons dealers, illegal immigrant smugglers, and Hamas affiliates. A sweeping operation was completed in Jenin. In Gaza, a suspected Israeli drone strike on a car near the Islamic University in Gaza City reportedly killed 2 individuals, and another drone strike on a tent in southern Khan Yunis allegedly killed 3 and injured 7. A Hamas delegation is expected in Cairo to discuss the implementation of the ceasefire agreement, specifically disarmament and Israeli withdrawal to the east of the Yellow Line. Mediators are awaiting Israel's response to a revised "Peace Council" document.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations in southern Lebanon included an operative opening fire on Israeli reservists in Bint Jbeil, seriously wounding one and killing an Oketz canine unit dog. In response, Israeli troops captured one Hezbollah Radwan Force member and shot another dead in the same area. Israeli forces reportedly conducted a series of building demolitions in the Shi'ite village of Taybeh in southern Lebanon. An Israeli drone was spotted on a rooftop in Toulin village. Defense Minister Katz reaffirmed Israel's intent to remain in its security zone in Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed and the threat to northern residents is removed.

SYRIA & IRAQ
A drone attack struck a camp belonging to an Iranian-Kurdish opposition group northeast of Erbil, Iraq. Sirens were activated at US military bases in Iraq, including Harir in Erbil, Victory base near Baghdad airport, and Al-Tawhid 3 base in Baghdad. Quds Force commander Ismail Qaani met with Abu Alaa Al-Wala'i, leader of Kata'ib Sayyid al-Shuhada militia, in Iraq during the funeral events for Ali Khamenei. US Secretary of State announced President Trump's intent to revoke Syria's designation as a state sponsor of terrorism, citing new economic opportunities.

GULF STATES
The region experienced direct military engagement and heightened alert levels. The Jordanian army intercepted 8 missiles launched towards the Kingdom, leading to the temporary closure of Amman's airport and a "shelter in place" order from the US Embassy in Jordan. Kuwait's military reported intercepting 4 ballistic missiles and 10 drones, with one person injured and material damage from falling debris. Bahrain's Ministry of Defense confirmed intercepting several Iranian aerial attacks and declared its forces to be on the highest defensive readiness. Alarms also sounded in Qatar, which the Iranian Army claimed was due to targeting a satellite antenna (early warning site). Diplomatically, Qatar's Foreign Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani discussed recent escalations with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi, condemning attacks on merchant ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Both Qatar and Saudi Arabia emphasized the necessity of dialogue to contain regional tensions. A US official indicated Bahrain participated in strikes on Iran. Movement through the Strait of Hormuz was reported to be almost completely halted.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Extensive US Strikes on Iran**: CENTCOM confirmed striking approximately 90 military targets across 5 Iranian provinces, causing 14 deaths and 78 injuries. Targets included the strategic Ak-Taqqa-Khan railway bridge in Golestan and infrastructure in Bushehr, Chabahar, Sirik, Iranshahr, Jask, and Abu Musa Island.
2.  **Iranian Retaliation on US Bases**: Iran's Army launched numerous suicide drones against US military installations in Kuwait (Patriot system), Qatar (satellite antenna), and Bahrain (fuel tanks). Kuwait reported intercepting 4 ballistic missiles and 10 drones, with 1 injury. Bahrain confirmed aerial attacks and high alert.
3.  **Strait of Hormuz Closure**: Movement through the Strait of Hormuz has "almost completely halted," as reported by Bloomberg. Iran's military and Parliament Speaker Qalibaf threatened its full closure if US attacks persist, asserting control over its navigation.
4.  **Khamenei Funeral in Mashhad**: The funeral procession for the deceased "Leader" Ali Khamenei took place in Mashhad, Iran, following his body's transport from Najaf, Iraq, with significant public turnout and the presence of Quds Force Commander Qaani.
5.  **IDF Operations in Southern Lebanon**: Israeli troops captured an elite Hezbollah Radwan Force member and killed another in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, during an operation that also involved an injured reservist and a killed Oketz dog.
6.  **US Shift on Iran Ceasefire**: President Trump declared the "ceasefire with Iran has at least temporarily ceased" and warned of a "20 to 1" retaliation for future Iranian aggression, indicating further strikes are probable.
7.  **Regional Spillover to Jordan and Iraq**: Jordan's army intercepted 8 Iranian missiles, leading to flight delays at Amman airport and a US Embassy "shelter in place" order. Sirens were activated at US bases in Iraq (Harir, Victory, Al-Tawhid 3).
8.  **IDF Troop Expansion Call**: IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir stressed the operational necessity and moral duty to "significantly expand the ranks of the IDF" to meet current and future missions.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high following the extensive US strikes and direct Iranian retaliation against US bases. The US declaration that the "ceasefire has at least temporarily ceased" and President Trump's threat of "20 to 1" retaliation signal a willingness for sustained and disproportionate military action. Iran's explicit threat to close the Strait of Hormuz, coupled with reported export surges to circumvent blockades, indicates a red line that, if crossed, would severely disrupt global energy markets and likely trigger further US military response aimed at ensuring freedom of navigation. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, the southern Iranian coastline, US military installations in Gulf states and Jordan, and southern Lebanon, where IDF operations against Hezbollah continue. Military postures are shifting, with Gulf states on high alert and the IDF advocating for significant troop expansion. The targeting of strategic infrastructure like railway bridges and potential (though denied by Iran) nuclear-related facilities escalates the gravity of the conflict.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US, through President Trump, has explicitly framed its actions as retribution for Iranian attacks on merchant ships in the Strait of Hormuz, declaring the ceasefire "at least temporarily ceased." Trump also claimed direct contact from Iranian officials seeking a deal, though expressed skepticism. Vice President Vance reinforced the US commitment to keeping the Strait of Hormuz open, threatening military action if Iran attempts to close it. US Secretary of State announced plans to remove Syria from the State Sponsors of Terrorism list. Qatar and Saudi Arabia engaged in diplomatic calls, urging dialogue to de-escalate regional tensions, with Qatar condemning attacks on merchant shipping. Germany, a NATO ally, has agreed to acquire and station Tomahawk cruise missiles from the US to address a strategic defense gap. The Czech Prime Minister stated his country would not participate in the EU's security support package for Ukraine. Russia continues its war in Ukraine, with President Putin rejecting negotiations and aiming for escalation, while halting diesel exports due to Ukrainian attacks. The US strike on the Ak-Taqqa-Khan railway bridge in Iran affects a key rail corridor for China and Russia. Turkey's President Erdogan dismissed Israeli opposition to selling F-35s to Turkey. Israel's mission to Venezuela continues providing earthquake recovery aid, presenting a national recovery plan.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions and unverified claims exist across the reporting. Iranian state media denied any attack on the Bushehr nuclear power plant, while multiple sources (N12, Kianmeli) reported a US missile impact in its vicinity. President Trump's claim that Iranian officials "called a little while ago" seeking a deal remains unverified by Iranian sources. An image shared by Trump depicting US strikes on Iran was identified by Faytuks Network as "old and AI-enhanced." Reporting on casualties from US strikes varies, with Iran's Health Ministry stating 14 dead and 78 injured, while other Iranian sources provided specific breakdowns like 3 fishermen killed in Sirik and 8 Navy/Air Force personnel killed, making a consolidated and definitive count difficult. Furthermore, while Kianmeli 1 claimed Iran launched missiles at US vessels in Hormuz, the official Iranian Army statement primarily focused on attacks on US land bases in the Gulf. The identity of the "martyred Leader" being buried is consistently referred to as "Ali Khamenei" by the raw intelligence, despite external general knowledge of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as the current Supreme Leader and the recent death of President Ebrahim Raisi. This discrepancy is noteworthy given the instruction to strictly adhere to the provided raw data. Propaganda indicators include Press TV's classification as a "propaganda arm" of the Iranian regime and its framing of events, as well as Trump's use of inflammatory language towards Iranian leadership. Reporting gaps include the precise types and full damage assessments of the weapons used by both sides, and comprehensive details on the broader implications of the "Islamabad MoU" and its alleged breach by both parties.
